title: 8 March women’s-rights protest in central Baku
location: Central Baku, near the Natavan monument
organizer: Feminist activists; JAMnews names Narmin Shahmarzade and Gulnara Mehtieva among organizers/activists; no organization identified
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown: neither opened report provides a numeric attendance estimate. JAMnews quotes an organizer saying police prevented a larger number from attending, without a count; the Equal Times search-only estimate remains unverified.

title.summary: Two opened reports describe a feminist March 8 action in central Baku.

start_date.summary: Zerkalo is dated March 8 and says activists acted “today”; JAMnews labels its archive item 08.03.2024 and describes the March 8 event.

start_precision.summary: The article gives the calendar day.

end_date.summary: No physical ending time/date is reported; left null.

location.summary: Zerkalo places the action in central Baku near the Natavan monument; JAMnews describes a picket before that monument.

scope.summary: A single local action in central Baku is described; no nationwide organization is stated.

organizer.summary: Both reports describe feminist activists and organizers. JAMnews names Narmin Shahmarzade and Gulnara Mehtieva but no organizing organization.

demands.summary: The opened reports support demands concerning women’s rights, violence against women, early marriage, equal rights and social/economic freedom; JAMnews also reports discussion of femicide, discrimination against LGBTQ people, hate crimes, environmental issues and women affected by war, with disabilities, or single mothers.

participants_original.summary: Neither opened report gives a number. JAMnews reports an organizer’s statement that police prevented a larger number of participants from attending but does not quantify it. Equal Times’ roughly-20 search snippet remains unverified.

participants_min.summary: No numeric minimum can be established from the opened reports; JAMnews says police prevented a larger number attending without quantifying.

participants_max.summary: No numeric maximum can be established from the opened reports; JAMnews says police prevented a larger number attending without quantifying.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both opened reports lack a numeric count. JAMnews quotes an organizer saying police prevented a larger number attending but gives no number; the Equal Times snippet suggesting roughly 20 is unverified. The >=50 criterion remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: The story does not describe protester violence; value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Zerkalo reports police blocked approaches and removed placards, and says no arrests occurred. JAMnews reports police blockades, some participants detained en route then allowed in, an organizer briefly detained and released, and police trying to take placards. Because terminology/outcomes differ, formal arrest classification remains unknown. Neither account establishes beating, shooting, killing, or dispersal.

eligibility.summary: Two opened reports establish the action but neither provides numeric attendance; eligibility remains pending_threshold.

notes.summary: Zerkalo credits Turan, so it is not independent of a Turan account. JAMnews is a separate publication and provides a distinct report, but no origin attribution establishes further independence. Neither resolves the threshold.

open_questions.summary: Attendance threshold unresolved; organizing organization, state target, precise end, and campaign continuity remain unspecified.

notes: Zerkalo credits Turan. A separate JAMnews account confirms the March 8 Baku picket, describes access blocking, brief detentions and placard interference, and quotes an organizer saying police prevented a larger number from attending without giving a number. Zerkalo says there were no arrests; JAMnews describes brief detention/release, so formal arrest classification is unknown. No numeric crowd size or evidence establishing the >=50 threshold.
open_questions: What organization convened the action, if any?
Were organizers explicitly directing demands to Azerbaijan’s government or a specific state body?
Did the action end the same day, and was it part of an ongoing campaign?
Can another independent contemporaneous source provide a numeric attendance estimate?
